- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope to prevent overhang.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates momentum — cap forecast growth at 3–5% above recent 7-day average.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model exhibits mean reversion bias — forecast should be anchored to 14-day moving average rather than 30-day trend.
- If true outcome is significantly below forecast (e.g., >10% gap), check if sentiment was positive recently — if so, reduce forecast by 2–5% to reflect cooling sentiment.
- If true outcome is significantly above forecast (e.g., >10% gap), check if sentiment was negative — if so, increase forecast by 2–5% to reflect sentiment reversal.
- Model tends to lag in early days of new sentiment shifts — adjust forecast to align with sentiment change 2–3 days ahead of actual price movement.
